8537-lonesome-land.title: Lonesome Land
8537-lonesome-land.creator: B. M. Bower
8537-lonesome-land.description: A book by B. M. Bower. But men will live anywhere if by so doing there is money to be gained, and so a town snuggled up against the northern rim of the bench land, where the bleakness was softened a bit by the sheltering hills, and a willow-fringed creek with wild rosebushes and chokecherries made a vivid green background for the meager huddle of little, unpainted buildings.

arxiv-2106-12839.title: Visualizing Graph Neural Networks with CorGIE: Cor responding a G raph to I ts E mbedding
arxiv-2106-12839.creator: Zipeng Liu, Yang Wang, Jürgen Bernard, Tamara Munzner
arxiv-2106-12839.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Zipeng Liu, Yang Wang, Jürgen Bernard, Tamara Munzner. Graph neural networks (GNNs) are a class of powerful machine learning tools that model node relations for making predictions of nodes or links. GNN developers rely on quantitative metrics of the predictions to evaluate a GNN, but similar to many other neural networks, it is difficult for them to understand if the GNN truly learns characteristics of a graph as expected.

arxiv-2405-19425.title: Adaptive In-conversation Team Building for Language Model Agents
arxiv-2405-19425.creator: Linxin Song, Jiale Liu, Jieyu Zhang, Shaokun Zhang, Ao Luo, Shijian Wang, Qingyun Wu, Chi Wang
arxiv-2405-19425.description: Abstract Leveraging multiple large language model (LLM) agents has shown to be a promising approach for tackling complex tasks, while the effective design of multiple agents for a particular application remains an art. It is thus intriguing to answer a critical question: Given a task, how can we build a team of LLM agents to solve it effectively?

arxiv-2410-09138.title: Resolution of an Erdős’ problem on least common multiples
arxiv-2410-09138.creator: Stijn Cambie
arxiv-2410-09138.description: Abstract Erdős posed the question whether there exist infinitely many sets of consecutive numbers whose least common multiple ( lcm \lcm ) exceeds the lcm \lcm of another, larger set with greater consecutive numbers. In this paper, we answer this question affirmatively by proving that the ratio of the lcm \lcm ’s can be made arbitrarily large.

arxiv-2503-22068.title: A Proposal for Networks Capable of Continual Learning
arxiv-2503-22068.creator: Zeki Doruk Erden & Boi Faltings
arxiv-2503-22068.description: Abstract We analyze the ability of computational units to retain past responses after parameter updates, a key property for system-wide continual learning. Neural networks trained with gradient descent lack this capability, prompting us to propose Modelleyen , an alternative approach with inherent response preservation.

arxiv-2512-00101.title: The Bottleneck Birthday Problem
arxiv-2512-00101.creator: Chijul B. Tripathy
arxiv-2512-00101.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Chijul B. Tripathy. We introduce a fun problem that can be considered as a variant of the classic birthday problem, the Bottleneck Birthday Problem ( BBP ) . It is stated as: what is the maximum number of people we have to choose so that no day of the year has more than r ≥ 1 r\geq 1 birthdays incident on it with probability at least 1/2?

pmc-11352649.title: Dorsal Anterior Cingulate Cortex Coordinates Contextual Mental Imagery for Single-Beat Manipulation during Rhythmic Sensorimotor Synchronization
pmc-11352649.creator: Maho Uemura, Yoshitada Katagiri, Emiko Imai, Yasuhiro Kawahara, Yoshitaka Otani, Tomoko Ichinose, Katsuhiko Kondo, Hisatomo Kowa, Ernesto Pereda
pmc-11352649.description: Flexible pulse-by-pulse regulation of sensorimotor synchronization is crucial for voluntarily showing rhythmic behaviors synchronously with external cueing; however, the underpinning neurophysiological mechanisms remain unclear. We hypothesized that the dorsal anterior cingulate cortex (dACC) plays a key role by coordinating both proactive and reactive motor outcomes based on contextual mental imagery.

pmc-11373837.title: Identification of Schistosoma haematobium and Schistosoma mansoni linear B-cell epitopes with diagnostic potential using in silico immunoinformatic tools and peptide microarray technology
pmc-11373837.creator: Arthur Vengesai, Marble Manuwa, Herald Midzi, Masimba Mandeya, Victor Muleya, Keith Mujeni, Isaac Chipako, Takafira Mduluza
pmc-11373837.description: IntroductionImmunoinformatic tools can be used to predict schistosome-specific B-cell epitopes with little sequence identity to human proteins and antigens other than the target. This study reports an approach for identifying schistosome peptides mimicking linear B-cell epitopes using in-silico tools and peptide microarray immunoassay validation.

pmc-11459960.title: HELLO: a protocol for a cluster randomized controlled trial to enhance interpersonal relationships and team cohesion among ICU healthcare professionals
pmc-11459960.creator: Elie Azoulay, Nancy Kentish Barnes, Sheila Nainan Myatra, Maria-Cruz Martin Delgado, Yaseen Arabi, Carole Boulanger, Giovanni Mistraletti, Maria Theodorakopoulou, Vernon Van Heerden, José-Artur Paiva, Oktay Demirkýran, Gabriel Heras La Calle, Abdulrahman Al Fares, Gaston Burghi, Guy Francois, Anita
pmc-11459960.description: BackgroundMental health symptoms among healthcare professionals (HCP) in intensive care units (ICUs) are a significant concern affecting both HCP well-being and patient care outcomes. Cross-sectional studies among members of the European Society of Intensive Care Medicine (ESICM) report up to 50% burnout rates. Determinants of burnout include communication, team cohesion, psychological support, and well-being promotion.

pmc-12693682.title: A Recipe for Resilience: A Systematic Review of Diet and Adolescent Mental Health
pmc-12693682.creator: Jade E Tucker, Anthony M Brennan, David Benton, Hayley A Young, Carol Johnston
pmc-12693682.description: Background/Objectives: Adolescence is a critical period of vulnerability for the onset of mental health difficulties, presenting an urgent need for scalable prevention strategies. Diet is a universal, modifiable factor, yet its evidence base remains inconsistent. This systematic review synthesised evidence from controlled trials and prospective cohort studies investigating the relationship between diet and mental health in adolescents aged 10–19 years.

pmc-12849683.title: Concomitant infectious foci in community-acquired bacterial meningitis: the clinical impact of concomitant spondylitis and endocarditis
pmc-12849683.creator: Takafumi Hosokawa, Shoji Ogawa, Taiki Sawai, Yukiyo Yoshimoto, Yoshitsugu Nakamura, Shin Ota, Takahiko Hirose, Hideto Nakajima, Shigeki Arawaka
pmc-12849683.description: BackgroundCommunity-acquired bacterial meningitis has been linked to concurrent infectious foci in certain cases. However, reports specifically addressing concomitant infectious foci in patients with community-acquired bacterial meningitis, particularly in recent years, remain scarce. Moreover, the distinct characteristics of various types of concomitant infectious foci in bacterial meningitis cases have yet to be fully elucidated.

pmc-13586851.title: Spatial architecture of tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes adds predictive value beyond stromal TIL density for neoadjuvant response in triple-negative breast cancer
pmc-13586851.creator: Ke Yang, Hua Huang, Wei Shen, Yang Liu, Daxin Gao, Tian Hao, Haiyu Zhou, Yonghong Huang
pmc-13586851.description: BackgroundStromal tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes (TILs) are established biomarkers in triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC), but conventional density-based assessment does not capture their spatial relationship to tumor nests. We evaluated whether an H&E-derived spatial architecture index (SAI) provides predictive information beyond stromal TIL density for pathologic complete response (pCR) after neoadjuvant therapy.
